correctness.rationale: Steiner symmetrization about an axis of the contained body preserves containment, area, and convexity, and a direct slice calculation shows that a centrally symmetric supersets center is orthogonally projected onto the axis. Alternating two nonparallel axes drives centers to their intersection; compactness gives a same-area centered limit. The centered inclusion-minimum is then exactly \(\operatorname{conv}(K\cup(2o-K))\). For regular odd polygons, adjoining antipodes produces the regular \(2n\)-gon and the exact area ratio is \(\cos(\pi/n)\). The packaged coordinate checker verifies the parity/hull identities through \(n=101\), but the infinite theorem rests on the proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The result supplies both a structural optimization theorem for every planar two-axis convex body and a complete closed formula for a canonical family. It identifies the minimizing supersets rather than only their areas and gives the exact quadratic symmetry deficit for odd regular polygons. The two-axis hypothesis is geometrically natural and the conclusion directly simplifies a classical global center optimization, so the contribution is not an arbitrary special case or a mere numerical evaluation.
